packageRules.description: Pinned to the version pi ships. Pi's extension loader aliases typebox to its own bundled copy, so our declaration only types what pi executes and must match it. It moves when pi moves, not on Renovate's schedule; the typebox pin test reports when that happens.

@types/node describes the runtime, so it tracks the Node these packages run on rather than the newest DefinitelyTyped release. Types from a later major describe APIs that are not there and hide ones that were removed, and tsc believes them either way. The ceiling follows the major of the `engines` floor in package.json, not the newer Node that mise.toml runs, so raise it when that floor moves.

mise generates the files under .mise/locks when it locks a tool, and Renovate's mise manager regenerates them with each bump. Left on, the npm manager also reads the npm-renovate sidecar's package.json and bumps it alone, out of step with its aube-lock.yaml and mise.renovate.lock's digest
Renovate supports only Node 24 (its engines say ^24.11), so the toolset its own tasks run in stays there while the repo moves on

Pi releases land as soon as they ship. Extensions run inside whatever pi the user has installed, so our types and smoke tests must track the newest release rather than wait out the npm release-age gate. Bumping raises the package.json floor too, so the declared range names the pi we actually build against.
